system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Glucose transporter type 1 deficiency syndrome (SLC2A1-related Glut1 deficiency)
mechanism: Insufficient GLUT1-mediated glucose transport across the blood-brain barrier causes cerebral energy deficiency and hypoglycorrhachia despite a normal blood glucose concentration.
vignette: A 2-year-old girl has recurrent seizures, developmental delay, and episodic ataxia that is more noticeable before meals. Serum glucose is normal. Cerebrospinal fluid obtained after a short fast shows a markedly reduced glucose concentration with low-normal lactate. Brain MRI shows no structural abnormality.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractors: Fanconi-Bickel syndrome due to GLUT2 deficiency
distractor_notes: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency can cause neurologic disease and lactic acidosis; it does not characteristically produce isolated hypoglycorrhachia with normal blood glucose from impaired blood-brain-barrier glucose transport.
MCAD deficiency causes fasting hypoketotic hypoglycemia and systemic metabolic decompensation rather than normal blood glucose with disproportionately low CSF glucose.
GLUT2 deficiency causes Fanconi-Bickel syndrome with hepatic glycogen accumulation and renal Fanconi syndrome, not the classic brain-energy/hypoglycorrhachia phenotype of GLUT1 deficiency.
Maple syrup urine disease is a branched-chain amino-acid catabolic defect with neonatal/episodic encephalopathy and characteristic biochemical abnormalities, not isolated low CSF glucose.
key_expl: Glut1 deficiency syndrome is a disorder of brain energy metabolism caused by insufficient glucose transport across the blood-brain barrier. The key laboratory clue is hypoglycorrhachia in the setting of a normal blood glucose concentration, together with early seizures and developmental/movement abnormalities.
objective: Recognize GLUT1 deficiency syndrome from neurologic dysfunction plus low CSF glucose despite normal blood glucose.
